topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines the speaker's background, and defines the learning objectives regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Concepts of cancer etiology: genetics, environment, and chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational drivers of cancer by examining how endogenous mutations, inherited predispositions, and environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk and geographic variation.

topics.label: Pathogen-induced carcinogenesis and Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how infectious agents contribute to malignancy, illustrating the concepts with the multifactorial pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how dietary toxins, radiation, and xenobiotically activated chemical compounds cause direct and indirect DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, focusing on the distinction between initiators and promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental vulnerability.

topics.label: Methods for identifying and assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine whether specific exposures and substances cause cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and everyday risk-benefit balancing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by framing carcinogenic exposure within everyday risk-benefit decision-making and summarising the main themes.
